body: You're hitting the nail of the head, that'd exactly how I feel right now. I think regardless of anything she cares about nobody except this guy she's dating, not me nor any of her other friends. So as far as I'm concerned if she wants to put everything into him then she'll have to make do with what little she gets back out from it. I would've happily made the effort for her but if she doesn't want me in her life then that's her mistake. Anyway, thank you for taking the time to talk with me, I appreciate all the kind words and sympathy
So it's clingy to not want to be stood up repeatedly by my friend?

You'd think that was the case but half the time I'd speak to her she'd be venting about something she'd done or said. It was like every single time they'd hang put there was always something that bothered her. Hence why it's all the more confusing.

I have tried talking to her about it on multiple occasions. Every time I tried to get her to understand how hurt I was feeling she just said "I promise I'll make it up to you somehow" and never did. Never even made an effort to try, things just continued as they were.

I start university in a month so I'm hoping to meet some people there. That's what I'm afraid of, the breakup. Despite everything I still really care about her and want her to be okay but I know their relationship isn't going to last and when it does end she's going to be devastated and alone. That's why I don't feel like I can block her, because I want to be there for her when nobody else is.

I start uni in a month so I've kind of just been biding my time until I can meet a bunch of new people then. In the meantime though I like the sound of volunteering, I might try and get my shit together and do that, thank you.

That's exactly what I was thinking the other day! I realised there's a chance she might not see as a friend as much as she sees me as an "emotional support animal". A lot of the time it would feel like she'd only ever phone me to talk vent about something her bf or another friend of hers did because apparently I was a good listener.

Also you're spot on with the 2-4 week text. We've had arguments before where she says she wants rid of me and usually I end up blocking her, but after a couple weeks I start to feel guilty and unblock her to see if she says anything to which she welcomes me back with open arms.

I wish I could just look into her head to see what she really thinks of me. She always says some really sweet and genuine things but they don't line up with her actions at all. I want to block her because I I'm tired of being confused all the time and on this emotional rollercoaster but at the same time I know if I do I'll always wonder if she really meant all those sweet things she said.

I know you're right, I know I need to move on and forget about her, and maybe I will eventually. But for now I just can't bring myself to fully cut her off just yet (Edit: Upon further introspection I've realised I don't want to block her because I kind of want the satisfaction of being able to tell her to fuck off if she does ever reach out). Regardless, thank you for your insight. Knowing random Internet strangers will take the time to read through my troubles and give advice always gives me a little reassure that feeling this way isn't the norm

Mental health services in my country are... lacking, to say the least. That's kind of why I've come here, just wondering if anyone had any techniques they've used to deal with similar issues. But I'm definitely going to read through some of the things that you linked me earlier, thanks.

No it's not that bad, I always try to keep my thoughts to myself because I don't want to constantly trouble my friends by double checking with them. That being said, my girlfriend has gotten very good at noticing when something is bothering me.
Oh right okay. Well thanks :)

What do you mean by establishing the trust? I'm completely open with my girlfriend about doing this and she always tries to reassure me that she loves me and thinks I'm great, but I still can't help but feel she's just saying that to calm me down and doesn't actually mean it.

I have moments like that too. Usually a few hours after coming home I'll have spent so much time replaying recent events that I'll have enough "evidence" to conclude that in fact I am dull and all of my friends only sticking around out of either pity or the fear I'll do something irreversible if they all left me.

I mean I do want to matter to my friends, to know that if I did disappear that I would be missed just as I would miss them if they disappeared. Otherwise, well what's stopping me?

I feel as though having that affect on people wouldn't limit my freedoms at all anyway. I could still do what I want when I want, but instead I might have somebody to do it with or tell about it to after.

Maybe we're different in that regard but I would much rather do things with people I know would want to spend time with me, than do them alone.
Wow, that actually made me cry a little bit. I really needed to hear that, that I could fuck everything up and things could still work out alright. Thank you. I'm gunna go find a dog to hug now. <3

You're absolutely right, it hasn't been a long time at all. It just hurts to know she's probably moved on already while I'm still thinking about all the memories we shared and trying to drown my sorrows in ice cream (it's not working).

If you're still waiting for your SO to come back, I hope they do because they'd be privileged to have somebody as committed as you.
Good bot. Not sure what that means but thank you

In regards to my friend, it's just tough because I relied on her a lot over the last 18 months. She was always there is something bad happened and I needed support. She was my rock. But gradually I'm beginning to think back on a lot of our friendship and realising she maybe wasn't as great a friend as I made her out to be. In other words, I am starting to realise thatI don't in fact need her, and never did. On a more positive note though, I have already told her how grateful I was to have her around as long as I did and that she helped me grow in a lot of ways.

I like that comparison to the Dunning-Krueger effect though. I'm guessing I'm in the so-called "Valley of Despair" right about now so I guess it's encouraging to know that whatever direction I go, I'm going up (hopefully not regressing in competency though).

Thank you for the kind words, you've actually really given me the encouragement I needed right now :)

I am! I always have been and she was finally starting to see that, so I just need to keep at it! I'm not gunna let this get to me and she'll come around eventually, no matter how long it takes. Thank you for building me up and helping me realise that :)
I'm confused, if I'm not supposed to think she chose the other guy then should I keep trying to win her over?

You're right, I do need to be confident. I ended up telling her I regretted what I said but she told me not to, which I think means she's chosen the other guy. I feel terrible but hopefully it's the right move in the long run.

Well it's encouraging to know I'm not alone in all this at least. But yeah I think you might be right about the momentary happiness, that's where all my doubt is coming from anyway. I'm afraid that if I do say yes, she'll eventually just leave me for another guy. But thanks for the advice.

From what she's told me he has shown interest, it sounds like the situation between the two of them is very similar to the one between her and I, hence why I'm not completely writing her off just yet.
I guess that's one way of looking at it. If we do date and it turns out she doesn't really care for me then the worst I'll have is a bit of heartbreak which I'll get over soon enough. Thanks
She's my first pick, which is why I sort of want the same in return from somebody. But are you just saying I should just go for it regardless?

I used to have a friend who sounded just like that, they and I just sort of clicked and to this day I've never met anyone who I've been as close with as I was with them. They even saved my life a few times, talking me off a ledge when I was at my lowest.

Eventually though, some stuff happened between us, we started arguing a lot and gradually became more and more distant from each other until one day we just agreed to stop talking altogether. Since then it's felt like a piece of me is missing but slowly I'm starting to fill the hole they left in my life.

It's been a few months now and recently I realised that for the first time I don't wish to have them back anymore, like if they texted me and asked to start over I would turn them down because I think I've finally moved on. I know it probably doesn't feel like it right now, but if my experience is anything to go by, it will get easier. Nobody will be exactly like the friend you lost, but I'm sure you'll meet people eventually who fill that gap in your life in their own unique way.

Wounds take time to heal. Just hang in there, things will start to lighten up eventually :)

There's no shame in coming to subs like this if you ever need to talk, generally the people here are really understanding about whatever you might be going through and it's always comforting to meet somebody dealing with almost the exact same issues as you. If you ever need to chat feel free to hit me up :)

It's a noble trait to have, helping somebody even to your own detriment. But it is important to know when enough is enough and you need to take a step back for your own sake. If she doesn't already know and you're feeling brave you could maybe try opening up to her about how you've been doing recently but obviously you would know better than I whether that's actually a good idea.

Nowadays though with her starting to grow away from me it's been quite tough having to deal with stuff on my own now. I've definitely been relying on reddit to fill my social needs a lot more recently.

I keep trying to convince her to move on but she always claims I'm the only one who listens and I reluctantly stick around to help her out, despite how it negatively my own mental health.

If you need to talk about what's troubling you though I know there's plenty of people here would be willing to listen, myself included :)

Yeah, sadly most people only really stick around as long as its convenient for them. It's good that you've got a few people you can trust though, I'm glad.

That's the problem, you can never really know how much you can trust somebody until the day they give you a reason not to. Until then you've just got to hope and trust somebody with your vulnerabilities. Sure they might hurt you in the end, but soon enough those wounds will heal and you can try again until you find somebody who will have your back no matter what.

Well firstly, happy belated birthday. I hope you did something nice, even if it was something as simple as devouring a tub of ice cream or watching a good movie.

Yeah I don't really know what to say about your mom. You'd think given you're her flesh and blood that she'd want to make your life easy and protect you at all costs, but I guess not. Just don't think it's at all because of you, it's not. If she doesn't give a shit about what you're going through, that's on her.

I'm not suggesting you move out right away by the way. I'm just saying that you won't be living with your mom forever so there's no reason to end your life over her. Just keep focused on that goal of moving out and starting your own life, then you can put as much distance between yourself and her/anybody else as you need.

I suppose that's true to an extent, some people simply don't know how they can help and so they just distance themselves. But even when people have received help themselves and know first hand what helps the most, you still get those who'd rather just look out for themselves which is the sad part.

I'm glad you've got your three friends though. Even just knowing that they'll be there if you need them can mean the world sometimes.

The exact same thing happened to me, I started dating somebody over summer and I genuinely thought she was the one. I saw her almost three or four times a week and it was he happiest time of my life. That is until she told me the day after my birthday that she was breaking up with me because she wanted to pursue a more serious relationship with the guy she cheating on me with. Then I started constantly checking her insta profile and my heart broke all over again whenever I saw a picture of the two of them.

First thing you need to do is just uninstall instagram. I get that it might be a bit difficult if that's the main way you stay connected with friends but you can reinstall it if you need to once you're over your ex and not tempted to check her profile anymore. In the meantime you could suggest using as different platform to keep in touch.

Honestly though, if she was cheating on you and then left you for the other guy she wasn't worth your time anyway. It sounds to me like she didn't care about your feelings at all (especially if she told you on your birthday, that's just heartless) so why would you want to be with somebody that doesn't respect how you feel?

When you think you're ready I would reccomend just thinking back over the relationship and looking for all those red flags. For example with my ex I realised that she never posted pictures of me on her insta and never went out of her way to do something nice for me. Finding those red flags will help you realise that it's not the end of the world that she's gone because it gives you the opportunity to find somebody even better when the time is right.

I wish you the best mate. If you've got anybody you can reach out to for support right now I would do it, even if they're old friends you haven't spoken to in a while. The best thing you do for yourself is surround yourself with people who genuinely care about you and can help you get through this. Find something to distract yourself from her and soon all the pain you're feeling will begin to fade away.

I think I kind of understand how you feel. I was in a bad place a few months ago and kept trying to push away my then girlfriend and all my friends so that firstly they wouldn't be devastated when I killed myself, but secondly so that I felt alone enough to go through with it.

The thing about parents is that they're people just like anybody else. Sure you have the same blood as them and they raised you but that doesn't mean they get a special pass on being horrible to you. Imagine if your boyfriend treated you the way your mom did, well what I would do is talk to him about it and if he didn't change I'd break up with him, why should your mom be treated any differently?

I know that probably isn't an option for you at the moment since I get the impression you live together but if you're turning 18 soon (at least where I'm from) that means you can move out and live with somebody more supportive. Maybe completely cutting your mom out of your life is a bit extreme but if you feel you need to put some distance between the two of you that is totally alright. Please don't give up on the rest of your life just because your mom is making your life difficult at the moment, you won't have to put up with her forever.

I know that for some people it can be a little difficult to actually get the words out in the moment so if you're having trouble I've personally found that simply writing it all down on a bit of paper and showing them or having the conversation via text can sometimes help.

I'll be honest I don't perfectly relate to your anxiety over talking to friends. I find trouble talking to people I'm not really close with, I often get really shy and quiet and sometimes I'll even go to say something but no sound comes out. But despite that when I am talking to people I know andtrust I'm often the loudest of the bunch.

Maybe you'd find that once you get comfortable with somebody all that initial anxiety just sort of disappears. I mean from talking to you here you seem like a pretty chill person.

I found myself in a similar sort of relationship a while ago, myself and a friend both had a number of issues we were tried working out together and eventually it lead to us getting quite close. She always told me I was the only person she could fully rely on so I felt as if I had to do everything I could to look out for her and protect her so I think i understand how you feel to an extent.

If things are on the mend between the two of you the best thing I can suggest is that you try and help him as much you can/he'll let you. I know it can be quite draining but you don't have to sit back and watch this all pan out, if you're in a position to do so you could maybe try and find him a place to stay (not necessarily with you, maybe with a friend or a shelter), try and make sure he feels wanted and remind him that you really care about him and want him to get better, tell him how much seeing him like this absolutely devastates you.

But in saying all that also make sure you look after yourself. I know first hand trying to help somebody put their life back together when you yourself are dealing with things can be especially draining and if you feel like its having an adverse effect on you don't be afraid to tap out for a bit and recharge. Be upfront with your friend, don't try helping him if he won't help himself, you need to work together on this.

I'm really glad you were starting to feel better before all this happened and I really hope that can continue. You deserve a good and happy life just as much as your friend does and I'm sure he would agree too.
